B.name: Conversation-native inference for voice agents
B.one_line: A vLLM KVConnector plugin plus session gateway that pins voice sessions predicted to return soon and cheaply restores the rest, sold on a measured sessions-per-GPU at p95 TTFT <= 300 ms — today a single-seed 1.5x on an L40S/7B with an 8 ms margin, unmeasured against current stock offload tiers, on H100, or on production-size models.
B.strongest_version: A voice-session-aware residency layer that runs inside the buyer's own vLLM (later SGLang) as a plugin, sells a single measured number — concurrent sessions per GPU at full-load-window p95 TTFT <= 300 ms — and ships the harness and raw logs so buyers reproduce it on their GPUs and transcripts. Its one genuinely new mechanism is actuating a per-request idle-window prediction as HBM pinning through the stock KVConnector delayed-free hook, which is the only configuration of five that moved the measured knee (seed 1, L40S, 7B, 1.5x, 8 ms margin); the contiguous pinned-slab restore path that kept N=300 stable where a 2025 LMCache collapsed is the supporting substrate. The honest proof is a four-baseline benchmark (vanilla vLLM, vLLM's native OffloadingConnector, LMCache 0.5.x, SGLang HiCache) with a shuffled-hint ablation, 3 seeds, on H100 with a 26-35B model and partner transcripts; if predicted-idle pinning beats client-fixed TTLs and stock LRU tiers by >= 2x there, the sessions-per-GPU number becomes a line-priced capacity guarantee no voice or KV vendor in the research publishes. If the H100 test dissolves the wall for 7B, the same code re-scopes to 30B models where the KV pool is small again, and the harness itself remains a publishable instrument.
B.weeks_to_proof: 10-14 weeks to a first credible public proof, defined as: median-of-3-seeds sessions-per-GPU at full-load-window p95 <= 300 ms on H100, with a 26-35B-class model, against vanilla vLLM 0.28, vLLM's native OffloadingConnector (lru/arc), LMCache 0.5.4 layerwise and SGLang HiCache, with a shuffled-hint ablation and at least one real-transcript trace set, raw events.jsonl published. Assumptions: 1-2 engineers; ~120-150 GPU-hours (~$1-2k on Modal at $1.95/hr L40S and $3.95/hr H100; more on bare metal minimums); a design partner supplies transcripts by week 4 (none exists today); the week-1 H100 arm-A test does not kill the L40S/7B framing — if it does, add 2-4 weeks for TP>1 and hybrid-attention connector work to re-scope to 30B-on-H100. The brief's 6-week plan is the build schedule, not the proof schedule; weeks 1-2 (port of an experimental API from vLLM 0.9.2 to 0.28.0) and week 4 (30B/TP>1) are the slip points.

C.name: Session-aware serving engine: one residency scheduler for every idle regime (hosted + BYOC)
C.one_line: A residency scheduler inside vLLM/SGLang (stock KV-connector hooks) plus a session router and control plane that decides per session, from predicted return time, context size and per-tier break-evens, whether KV stays in HBM, moves to RAM/NVMe, or is dropped; sold as a hosted session-addressed endpoint and as BYOC software/optimization engagements for voice and agent platforms and inference providers.

D.name: Document-VLM inference provider
D.one_line: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving an open VLM (Qwen2.5-VL-7B measured; Qwen3-VL-8B vendor-reported) at a measured document accuracy/cost operating point, billed per page and sold on a same-pages rerunnable benchmark; the 0.925-vs-0.880 DocVQA seed is real but relaxed-match on 200 pages, the "~40x cheaper" is a list-price model whose Qwen token count contradicts the repo's own measurement (corrected modeled ratio ~9-10x), and the in-model pruning moat sprint has no result.

E.name: Verifier-guided search inference for code (pass@16 quality at pass@4 cost)
E.one_line: A Morph-style specialized provider for coding agents: send a prompt plus tests, an in-engine verify-abort-refill scheduler returns the first passing sample; measured 2.63x fewer decode tokens and 2.12x faster at identical pass@16 on HumanEval with an 8B model, with the repo's own 'buyer-replicable' verdict confronted via pre-registered gates.

Measured but bounded and contradicted is C.
missing_founder_decisions: Licensing/monetization: the draft chose Apache-2.0 open-core with a per-GPU-month commercial control plane; alternatives are source-available/BSL, savings-share (Tensormesh's 30%-of-estimated-savings formula), or hosted-only (which the README excludes but edge/ and dexa_platform build).

Positioning: durability/governance-first for regulated and neocloud buyers vs a speed/cost positioning; the ledger currently contradicts the speed story, so the draft chose governance without evidence buyers pay for it.

Model class and TP scope: dense GQA 7-8B at TP=1 first (matches the evidence) vs the MoE/MLA/hybrid models at TP=8 that the workload research says customers run; this decides whether the product can touch a customer model in 6 weeks or 6 months.
Own the durable store vs build on LMCache's MP server / Mooncake Store / NIXL as the tier and sell only keying, policy and control plane.
Out-of-tree connector on an experimental API vs fork vLLM for scheduler-native prefetch and eviction ordering vs upstream contributions to vLLM's TieringManager RFC #38260 and SGLang RFC #27574.
Distribution channel: Kubernetes/llm-d well-lit path (the draft's choice) vs pip-only vs a Dynamo/NIXL plugin.
Proof metric: Preemption Survival Score (the draft's choice) vs a measured $/GPU-hour-saved metric that buyers actually pay on.
Go/no-go thresholds: '>= 2 of 5 design partners with audit log enabled', 'P99 <= 1.0x vanilla', '>= 2.0x at 64k' and the 10-day TP>1 limit are the draft's numbers; the founder sets them.
Which baseline configuration counts as 'well-configured' (LMCache layerwise-on with L2, OffloadingConnector with S3, Mooncake SSD) since that choice determines whether the benchmark can be won.

F.name: Portable, persistent KV state layer for self-hosters (open-core infrastructure software)
F.one_line: An Apache-2.0 vLLM/SGLang connector plus durable, tenant-keyed KV store that lets an agent session survive pod death and resume on any replica with the same output, sold with a commercial fleet control plane; the portability core is measured once in-engine at TP=1, the speed story is contradicted, and durability/governance are unbuilt.
F.strongest_version: The one property both repos proved at every context length is portable, lossless KV state: a vLLM process can load KV another process saved, skip prefill, and produce the same output, using the same connector seam LMCache, Mooncake and NIXL use, on an unmodified engine. Nothing in the research files sells that as an operator-owned object with tenant keying, retention policy and an audit log of who read which state; Mooncake and Dynamo ship tenant isolation but no project documents state-operation audit. The honest product is therefore a durability-and-governance layer with speed parity as a gate, proven on an independent harness (vllm bench serve, Mooncake traces) against baselines configured to survive, where the differentiation must show up in re-prefilled tokens, correctness and P99 under load rather than in survival itself. It is worth building only if two things measure true within ~10 weeks: greedy identity (or bounded divergence no worse than vanilla's own prefix hit) holds at 32k-128k on a real model, and a pipelined restore from a durable tier keeps P99 at or below vanilla under load. Both are single experiments the repos already have harnesses for; the customer-side unknowns (do self-hosters lose KV to restarts, do they pay per GPU for audit) are interview questions, not benchmarks.
F.weeks_to_proof: ~10 weeks to the first credible public proof at TP=1 (a Preemption Survival Score run on vllm bench serve + Mooncake traces vs vanilla, OffloadingConnector+S3 and LMCache 0.5.x layerwise, Llama-3.1-8B on A100 and H100, with KV-byte identity and greedy-divergence reported), assuming two senior engineers full-time, ~150-200 GPU-hours, no vLLM fork, and that the vLLM 0.28 port of the two pinned connectors (0.24.0 and 0.9.2) plus chunked-prefill/decode-block save and layer-pipelined async restore each take about a week. The draft's 6 weeks assumed TP>1 in one week against its own 10-day/60-multi-GPU-hour estimate; a TP=2/4 point adds 3-4 weeks and an MLA/hybrid model adds an unestimated amount.

H.name: Computer-use agent inference provider
H.one_line: An OpenAI-compatible, hosted-or-BYOC endpoint for screenshot-heavy computer-use agents: an open VLM at a screenshot-sized visual-token budget (322 tokens per 1280x800 frame vs 1,105 on GPT-4o), exact-frame dedup, session-affinity prefix warmth and per-request savings telemetry, with the ~40x headline shown to be modeled, the 7.3x redundancy prize bounded at ~2.3x, no OSWorld/WebArena validation yet, and a backend that is stock vLLM flags.

I.name: Fast Parse: the Morph playbook on document-to-structure
I.one_line: One specialized 2B-8B document-to-structure model (page image in; markdown + schema JSON out) served on a purpose-built vLLM path with visual-token budgeting, OCR-draft copy-speculation and constrained JSON decoding, priced per page — the Morph playbook applied to the one task where the repos hold a measured model-side result (Qwen2.5-VL-7B 0.925 vs GPT-4o 0.880 on DocVQA at 2.7x throughput).

J.evidence_grade_reason: The direction splits into sub-claims with different standings. Portability/losslessness is proven in-engine at TP=1 on OPT-125m and Qwen3-0.6B (A10G) and at HF level on Llama-3.1-8B/A100 (identical_output at 8k-64k). The restore-beats-re-prefill claim is contradicted inside the dexa repo: pinned-RAM LMCache restore wins 10-17x single-request at 4k-16k, while the only off-instance tier measured (Modal Volume, ~0.6-0.9 GB/s) loses 0.37x at 8k and 1.6-2.2x on P99 under 16-24-way concurrency, with the ~64k+ crossover never run because chunked-prefill save is missing. Everything that makes J distinct from the existing stateful-session direction (fast durable tier, resume storm behaviour, session registry, preemption handler, fleet manager, spot economics, customer context distribution) is unmeasured or unbuilt. All in-repo numbers are single-seed, TP=1, non-MLA, in-engine capped at 16k, and the concurrent evidence comes from 2.5k-token synthetic voice sessions on a 46 GB L40S with LMCache 0.3.2. Net: measured but bounded/contradicted, leaning D on the product-specific components.
missing_founder_decisions: Whether continuity-only (session-affinity router + transcript replay + deterministic continuation) is a product if the durable-tier gate fails, versus waiting for fp8/compaction to lower the gate, versus stopping.

vLLM vs SGLang as the engine to build on: the repos validated only vLLM; SGLang HiCache has L3 backends and open session-hint (pin/demote/TTL) RFCs; the dexa SGLang gate found SGLang ahead on branched decode. The draft picked vLLM silently.

Build a custom KV connector (the draft's architecture) vs build on LMCache 0.5.x (S3/GDS/NIXL backends exist today; 22 GB/s single-request measured) vs vLLM's native OffloadingConnector (object tier in developer preview). The dexa hosted product itself uses LMCache; the voice evidence favours a custom contiguous path only for LMCache 0.3.2.

Which model/TP class the public proof must cover: 7-8B at TP=1 (the only validated regime) vs 30B-A3B vs the buyer's GLM/Kimi-class MLA models at TP=8; the draft chose TP=1 for the proof and left the buyer's class to a later gate.

The reference price for the spot delta and therefore the cloud and GPU class: hyperscaler list (57-81% off H100/B200), neocloud on-demand (roughly zero delta), or hosted dedicated endpoints ($3.99-$8.00/H100-hr). The draft asserted 'interruptible H100 capacity' on one cloud in section 7 while leaving class open in section 11.
Whether to target the frontier-trace context regime (115-195K) or the open-weight guidance regime (32k) as the first segment, since the connector measurably loses in the latter.

Pricing shape: the draft asserted a two-meter model (session-hour + preemptible per-token) in section 8 while listing meter shape as open in section 11; 'per session-hour' vs 'per token' vs '30% of savings' remains the founder's call.
Whether a design-partner pilot should gate the benchmark or follow it; the draft scheduled two design partners in week 6 without evidence any exist.

Resume granularity: step-boundary-only resume (no decode-token KV saved, partial output re-prefilled) is an engineering default that affects the preemption UX during 45-minute turns; whether mid-step resume is required for the product is undecided.
Hosted vs BYOC vs OSS connector remains open; hosted is the only option that captures the spot margin, and the draft's MVP silently assumed hosted.
J.name: Preemptible-GPU inference made safe by portable session state
J.one_line: Run long-lived agent sessions on spot GPUs by making per-session KV portable to a durable tier and restorable on any instance; value is conditional on an unmeasured fast-durable-tier bandwidth at the customer's real context size, with only identical continuation proven below that crossover.
J.strongest_version: The honest strong form of J is a kill-and-resume proof, not a spot pitch: a session-addressed inference endpoint on interruptible GPUs where every session's KV is continuously written through to a tier that survives the instance, and a SIGKILL on instance A is followed by the session's next step on instance B with published resume p95, GPU-seconds, identity, and resume-storm GB/s, benchmarked against the buyer's own fallback (vanilla vLLM re-prefilling the transcript) and against LMCache/OffloadingConnector object tiers. The repos already give it what no competitor's docs describe together: in-engine cross-instance bit-identical restore at TP=1, a working V1 connector skeleton with async load and an adaptive load-vs-recompute policy, a contiguous pinned-slab transfer pattern that held N=300 where LMCache 0.3.2 collapsed, and a session API/control-plane skeleton. Its economics are expressible only because portable KV turns a preemption into bytes divided by bandwidth, which lets a preemptible per-token tier carry a restore SLO instead of Morph-style admission gating. The entire direction rests on one number nobody has measured, per-request restore bandwidth from a fast durable tier into vLLM paged KV at 64k-128k, and one distribution nobody has collected, the real context sizes of self-hosted open-weight agent steps; a one-week tier gate and two design-partner histograms decide whether J is a product or a determinism feature on a session-affinity router.
J.weeks_to_proof: 8-10 weeks to a credible public kill-and-resume benchmark at TP=1 on Llama-3.1-8B (three seeds, 8k-128k ladder, baselines vanilla vLLM prefix caching / LMCache 0.5.x S3+NVMe / vLLM OffloadingConnector, per-point tier GB/s). Assumptions: 1-2 engineers full-time; ~$3-6k GPU spend at Modal/spot rates (~150-250 GPU-hours incl. reruns); an S3/remote-NVMe backend for the dexa SessionStore or LMCache's backends lands in week 1 and the tier gate (>=0.5 GB/s per request at 128k) passes; chunked-prefill save (vllm_connector.py:608) plus the port of the voice connector's block-keyed contiguous-transfer path and a rebase from vLLM 0.24.0/0.9.2 to 0.28.0 take 2-3 weeks; generalizing the voice harness (text prompts, aiohttp abort, server-metric scraping, provenance, multi-seed) takes 2 weeks; runs and write-up 2 weeks. The draft's 6-week figure assumed the tier backend, harness generalization and API rebase were free and included a design-partner pilot with partners that do not exist in the research files. Add 4-6 weeks if the proof must include the buyer's TP>1/MLA model class; the hosted spot fleet, registry, preemption handler and streaming gateway are beyond the benchmark and not costed here. The week-1 gate can end the effort at week 1.

K.name: SessionBench + Resident-Slot SLA (benchmark-first, Wafer-motion session serving)
K.one_line: A benchmark-first company that publishes the sessions-per-GPU standard (SessionBench), ships the residency runtime that wins it, and sells warm session-slots with a stated retention window per slot-hour into voice and agent platforms that already price by concurrency — the Wafer engagements-plus-dedicated-endpoints motion applied to session-shaped serving, engine-neutral and upstream of candidates A/B/C.
